text:
Recent work supports separating topical relatedness from current usefulness. The 2024/2025 [intent-aware recommendation survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16350) emphasizes that intent changes across visits and within sessions; historical similarity therefore cannot establish present demand. A 2025 [relevance reannotation study](https://downloads.webis.de/publications/papers/parry_2025b.pdf) finds assessor disagreement and sensitivity to how information needs are specified. These findings support explicit temporal context and preserving disagreement rather than treating every annotation as definitive preference.

For the twenty-user audit, a proposed rubric is: “choose now” only with evidence supporting current actionable relevance; “related only” for supported connections without established current need; “explicit mismatch” only for an evidenced contradiction; “insufficient information” when decisive evidence is missing. Record separate reason codes—historical connection, recent-intent support, documented contradiction, missing description, unknown compatibility, unknown demand status—and attach history item IDs, timestamps, and exact title/description excerpts to each claim. Missing evidence must never become dislike. Compatibility, fulfilled demand, diversity preferences, and conformity remain unknown without explicit support. These are proposed operational rules, not validated labels supplied by the literature.

Calibrate annotators on shared examples, then independently double-annotate; report raw agreement, nominal Krippendorff’s alpha, label-confusion counts, and unresolved disagreements. Preserve “insufficient information” as a substantive label. The 2025 [abstention survey](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/) motivates reporting coverage alongside correctness among decided cases; confidence calibration requires independently adjudicated examples. [NIST’s caution on LLM relevance judgments](https://www.nist.gov/publications/dont-use-llms-make-relevance-judgments) reinforces treating automated audits as provisional evidence summaries. Keep this audit descriptive and separate from macro validation HR@10 model selection.
